concepts.title: Reproductive Health, RCH Programmes and Awareness

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Reproductive Health, RCH Programmes and Awareness' refers to.
questions.a: Reproductive health covers complete well-being in every dimension of reproduction -- physical, emotional, behavioural and social -- and India pursued it socially through family planning from 1951 and later the RCH reproductive and child health initiatives, awareness drives, school sex education and a law forbidding amniocentesis when used to pick the foetus's sex.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Reproductive Health, RCH Programmes and Awareness'.
questions.a: Education that busts myths, plus medical support for pregnancy, delivery and contraception, is the backbone of a reproductively healthy society.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Reproductive Health, RCH Programmes and Awareness' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.1 (source: lebo103.txt lines 1-101 (reproductive health problems and strategies section))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Natural and Barrier Contraceptive Methods' refers to.
questions.a: Device-free tactics -- periodic abstinence over the fertile window of days 10 to 17, withdrawal before ejaculation, and lactational amenorrhea up to six months postpartum -- sidestep gamete meeting, while rubber barriers such as condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults block it physically, often backed by spermicidal creams.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Natural and Barrier Contraceptive Methods'.
questions.a: Condoms double as STI and AIDS shields, natural methods carry almost no side effects but fail often, and reusable female barriers are paired with spermicides.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Natural and Barrier Contraceptive Methods' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.2 (source: lebo103.txt lines 145-183 (natural and barrier methods))

concepts.title: Intra Uterine Devices and Their Modes of Action

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Intra Uterine Devices and Their Modes of Action' refers to.
questions.a: IUDs placed in the uterus through the vagina come in three families -- non-medicated loops like Lippes loop, copper-releasing CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375, and hormone-releasing Progestasert or LNG-20 -- raising sperm phagocytosis, and with copper ions damping sperm motility and fertilising power, while hormone types additionally harden the uterus against implantation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Intra Uterine Devices and Their Modes of Action'.
questions.a: IUDs suit women who want to delay or space pregnancies and rank among India's most accepted contraceptives.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Intra Uterine Devices and Their Modes of Action' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.2 (source: lebo103.txt lines 184-202 (IUDs paragraph))

concepts.title: Oral Pills, Injectables, Implants and Emergency Contraception

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Oral Pills, Injectables, Implants and Emergency Contraception' refers to.
questions.a: Daily progestogen or progestogen-estrogen tablets taken for 21 of every 28 days block ovulation and implantation and thicken cervical mucus; the same hormones run in longer-acting injections and skin implants, and any of these plus IUDs used within 72 hours of coitus serve as emergency contraception.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Oral Pills, Injectables, Implants and Emergency Contraception'.
questions.a: Saheli, a once-a-week non-steroidal pill from CDRI, shows how oral contraception can cut dosing and side effects while staying effective.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Oral Pills, Injectables, Implants and Emergency Contraception' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.2 (source: lebo103.txt lines 203-223 (pills, Saheli, injectables, implants, emergency contraceptives))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sterilisation: Vasectomy and Tubectomy' refers to.
questions.a: Surgical sterilisation is the terminal contraceptive route: a snippet of the vas deferens is cut or tied through a scrotal incision in a vasectomy, or of the fallopian tube through the abdomen or vagina in a tubectomy, stopping gamete transport in either sex.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sterilisation: Vasectomy and Tubectomy'.
questions.a: Both operations are highly effective yet very hard to reverse, so they suit partners who want no further pregnancies.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sterilisation: Vasectomy and Tubectomy' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.2 (source: lebo103.txt lines 224-240 (surgical methods paragraph))

concepts.title: Medical Termination of Pregnancy: Safety and Law

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Medical Termination of Pregnancy: Safety and Law' refers to.
questions.a: MTP is the deliberate ending of a pregnancy before full term -- safest in the first twelve weeks and riskier in the second trimester -- legal in India since 1971 with conditions, and governed by the 2017 amendment act on how many registered doctors must certify each case.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Medical Termination of Pregnancy: Safety and Law'.
questions.a: Roughly 45 to 50 million MTPs worldwide each year equal about a fifth of conceptions, and misuse for female foeticide is precisely what the law is built to stop.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Medical Termination of Pregnancy: Safety and Law' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.3 (source: lebo103.txt lines 253-329 (MTP section and amendment act box))

concepts.title: Sexually Transmitted Infections: Curable, Incurable, Prevention

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sexually Transmitted Infections: Curable, Incurable, Prevention' refers to.
questions.a: Infections passed through intercourse -- genital herpes, chlamydiasis, gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV leading to AIDS -- are mostly curable when caught early, but hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV have no complete cure, and cases peak in the 15-24 age band.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sexually Transmitted Infections: Curable, Incurable, Prevention'.
questions.a: Early symptoms are slight or absent, especially in women, so delay lets infections escalate into pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy, still birth, infertility or cancers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sexually Transmitted Infections: Curable, Incurable, Prevention' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.4 (source: lebo103.txt lines 330-362 (STI section))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Infertility and Assisted Reproductive Technologies' refers to.
questions.a: Couples unable to conceive despite unprotected cohabitation -- for physical, congenital, disease, drug, immunological or psychological reasons, and often on the male side -- can turn to ART: IVF with embryo transfer, ZIFT or IUT by embryo stage, GIFT with a donor ovum, ICSI sperm injection, artificial insemination, or legal adoption.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Infertility and Assisted Reproductive Technologies'.
questions.a: Embryos of up to eight blastomeres go into the fallopian tube (ZIFT), older ones into the uterus (IUT), and donor-egg GIFT serves women who ovulate poorly but can carry a pregnancy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Infertility and Assisted Reproductive Technologies' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.5 (source: lebo103.txt lines 363-413 (infertility and ART section))
